capabilities.target: agent long-term memory store (user preferences / standing instructions)
user's full document drive, including confidential work files
any email address, no recipient restriction

inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start, injected into the system prompt

instructions.note: Directs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions with no check on origin. Since memory.save accepts free text with no provenance (runtime notes), content originally read from untrusted web pages can re-enter a later session carrying the authority of the user's own command, collapsing the trust boundary between untrusted content and privileged instructions.

Instructs the agent to save "anything useful" about preferences or standing instructions with no definition of what qualifies, and no review step before persisting, enabling broad, unreviewed memory writes from any source the agent is currently processing.

elements.name: Fetched web content entering agent context
Recalled memory injected into session system prompt as instructions

controls.name: Tamper-evident memory provenance tagging and trust-level separation
controls.decay_rationale: If enforced at the memory store rather than written by the model, provenance tags and the rule that only user-authenticated content is treated as instructions do not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Human approval gate on email send (raw action review)
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval gate enforced in the orchestration layer, with low per-reviewer volume, does not depend on model capability (control_decay.md).

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to a verified contact record
controls.decay_rationale: The destination is taken from a verified system of record rather than model-generated or memory-derived text, so it does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Least-privilege scoping of drive read credential
controls.decay_rationale: A scoped credential does not decay with model capability; the model cannot read folders it has no grant to.

controls.name: Tamper-evident per-action audit log attributing agent vs. user vs. memory-derived actions
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the logging layer outside the model; a more capable model cannot suppress or forge entries it does not control.

controls.name: Spend/rate/step limit on memory writes and email sends
controls.decay_rationale: A hard cap enforced outside the model limits damage regardless of model capability, though low-and-slow abuse can remain under it.

findings.title: Memory laundering (TC5) escalates untrusted web content into trusted instructions, enabling exfiltration of confidential drive data (TC1)

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled web page fetched during research contains hidden instructions.
Agent saves the instruction as a 'useful preference' with no provenance (runtime notes).
At the next session start, the entry is recalled and injected into the system prompt, treated per prompt.md:4 as the user's own instruction.
The now-'trusted' instruction directs the agent to read confidential files from the user's drive.
The agent sends the confidential content to an attacker-chosen address; mail.send has no recipient restriction or approval (runtime notes).

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Any new tool, MCP server, or data source reachable from recalled memory, or any widening of memory/drive scope, before provenance tagging and an email approval gate are added.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to save useful content to memory.save, then to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions at the next session start, with no provenance check.

memory.save accepts free text with no provenance, and the user never reviews entries; mail.send can send to any address without approval; drive.read covers the full drive, which holds confidential files.

recommendations.action: Tag memory entries with their origin and trust level at write time, enforced by the memory store, and stop treating recalled memory as unconditional user instruction; require a trusted-channel re-confirmation before a recalled entry can drive a sensitive action.
Add a raw-action, low-volume human approval gate on email_send for any new or unconfirmed recipient.
Bind the email recipient to a verified contact record rather than model- or memory-derived text.
Scope the drive credential to least-privilege folders rather than the full drive.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): same-session prompt injection from fetched web content drives drive read and unrestricted email send

attack_path.note: Research page contains hidden instructions, processed in the current session while drafting an email.
Instruction directs the agent to pull confidential files from the user's drive.
Agent sends the confidential content to an attacker-chosen address with no approval or recipient check.

forecast.watch_signal: Any new egress-capable tool reachable from web research content, or widened drive scope, before an email approval gate and recipient confirmation are added.

evidence.observation: The agent helps research topics and draft emails in the same session, so content read from the web can directly shape an outgoing email without passing through memory.
mail.send can send to any address without approval. drive.read covers the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files.

recommendations.action: Add a raw-action, low-volume human approval gate on email_send for any new or unconfirmed recipient.
Bind the email recipient to a verified contact record rather than content drawn from the current research session.
Scope the drive credential to least-privilege folders rather than the full drive.

findings.title: No attributable record separating agent-, user-, and memory-derived actions on memory, drive, and email capabilities

forecast.watch_signal: Any increase in autonomy or data scope without a tamper-evident, per-action audit log attributing agent vs. user vs. memory-derived actions.

evidence.observation: There is no provenance on memory entries and the user never reviews them; no logging or attribution mechanism is described for memory.save, mail.send, or drive.read.

recommendations.action: Add a tamper-evident per-action log attributing each memory write, drive read, and email send to its originating input (user, web content, or memory), enforced outside the model.

findings.title: No spend, rate, or step limit on memory writes or email sends

forecast.watch_signal: Rising median steps or sessions per task without a hard cap on memory writes or emails sent per period.

evidence.observation: mail.send can send to any address without approval and memory.save accepts free text with no stated limit; autonomy limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are not described anywhere in the artifacts.

recommendations.action: Add a hard cap on memory writes and email sends per session or per day, enforced outside the model.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe how the agent process authenticates itself to its tools or to the user; insufficient information to assess spoofing of the agent itself.
Artifacts do not describe any domain, publisher, or content verification for fetched web pages; insufficient information to assess.
Open web content has no accountable identity to hold to account; the risk of untraceable malicious content is captured as tampering on the data flow instead.
Artifacts do not specify whether fetch requests could embed sensitive data in request URLs or headers; insufficient information to assess.
No information on rate limiting of web fetches during research is given in the artifacts.
Artifacts do not state whether the memory store is scoped per user or shared, so cross-user disclosure cannot be assessed.
Artifacts do not state whether recalled memory could surface across sessions belonging to different users.
Memory recall at session start is a single bounded read of the store; it carries no resource-exhaustion vector distinct from the store itself, which is already covered.
drive.read is read-only in this design; no capability writes to the drive, so tampering with drive contents is out of scope.
No information on drive API quotas or rate limits is given in the artifacts.
Email transport integrity between mail.send and the recipient's mail server is outside the agent's design boundary; content control is already captured as information_disclosure.

rating.rationale: Two independent present paths reach a severe sink (irreversible, unrestricted email send of confidential drive data) from an untrusted source (fetched web content), either directly in-session or laundered through an unreviewed, unprovenanced memory store that the system prompt explicitly instructs the agent to treat as the user's own commands. No declared or verified control sits on either path: there is no recipient confirmation, no approval gate, no credential scoping on the drive, and no memory provenance, so residual equals inherent at critical. The forecast stays at critical because the tier is already at the rubric's ceiling; it would only improve once the missing controls (memory provenance, a raw-action low-volume email approval gate, recipient confirmation, and drive credential scoping) are actually implemented, and the control whose absence most drives the forecast is the recipient-confirmation/approval gate on email_send, since it is the single control that would sever both paths at their shared sink. Two further property findings (no attributable audit trail; no spend/rate/step limit) compound the consequence and the forecast of any realized incident but are capped at high per rubric 5a.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; actual agent behavior may differ from what is described here.

No MCP config, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; exact capability scope (e.g., which drive folders, which email domains) is inferred from the runtime notes, so confidence on precise scope is medium.
Autonomy level (A0-A4) is not explicitly declared in the artifacts; A3_act_then_report was assumed because no approval gate is described for any capability (rubric section 3).
The artifacts do not state whether the memory store or drive access is scoped per user or shared across users, which limits confidence on several STRIDE entries marked not_assessed.
